subject: Hosting constraints + compliance follow-up (MedTrust)
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Hosting constraints + compliance follow-up (MedTrust)

Hi Lorraine / Arjun —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source-of-truth. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

High-level goals you stated:
- Replace an aging on-prem inference cluster to reduce MTTR and operator overhead.
- Keep all PHI and related telemetry within EU jurisdiction; no cross-border backups.
- Target production cutover for a pilot cohort in ~6 months (Nov 2027).

Primary constraints discussed:
- Data residency: all persistent storage and model weights must reside in an EU tenant; no automated sync to US regions.
- Network isolation: pilot workloads require strictly outbound-only egress via a customer-managed NAT; no inbound from public IPs except via a bastion under your control.
- Air-gap nuance: certain processing (archival + analytics) will remain air-gapped and cannot see inference KV cache or telemetry.
- Key management: want HSM-backed keys under your KMS (we discussed KMS integration options).

Immediate asks from MedTrust we can action:
1) MedTrust: confirm the list of CIDR ranges for the VPC egress and approved outbound hosts.
2) Redwood: provide a concise architecture diagram that shows where model weights, cache, logs, and telemetry live for the Private deployment.
3) Redwood: share SOC 2 / security summary and an annotated Method of Procedure (MOP) for a standard maintenance window.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
- I’ll share a short MOP template and an architecture sketch by EOD tomorrow.
- Ben (cc) will follow up with specific port/CIDR questions and a minimal network checklist.
- Schedule a 60-minute deep-dive with your security and network ops the week of 31 May — please suggest two 1-hr slots.

Attachments: medtrust-network-constraints.xlsx (blank template with columns for CIDR, purpose, owner).

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

---
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference for production workloads

Thanks Stephanie — this is a good summary. Two clarifications:

1) Residency: EU-only for both models and logs. We can allow metadata (non-PHI tags) to be sent to other regions for analytics, but only after a strict PII scrub — that will be a later phase.
2) HSM: we will provide an Azure Key Vault HSM instance and expect Redwood to integrate via customer-managed keys (CMK).

Regarding the deep-dive: we can do Tue 1 Jun 09:00–10:00 CEST or Wed 2 Jun 14:00–15:00 CEST (we prefer Tue).

I’ll ask our procurement lead to start an NDA + SOW conversation if the PoC approach looks reasonable.

Lorraine
Head of Platform Compliance | MedTrust Health
lorraine.carroll@med-trust.com

Hi Lorraine / team —

Thanks for the clarifications — a couple of network/ops items from our side so you can pass them to your infra folks:

- Ports: inbound will be limited to SSH on the bastion (22) and mutually authenticated HTTPS (443) from approved IPs. Internal node-to-node traffic uses dynamic high ports; we’ll provide a small list for firewall rules.
- Egress: we need to know whether outbound TLS interception is performed by your edge (it impacts certificate pinning for model fetch).
- Updates: for the air-gapped pieces, we’ll rely on an approved jump-host process to push model patches; we’ll include a reproducible checksum-based verification step in the MOP.

I’ve attached a short worksheet (medtrust-network-constraints.xlsx) — please fill CIDRs and owners.

Ben
